metadata.title: Plan And Design Template
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Complete template design including purpose, parameters, steps, and flow diagram

output.description: Complete template design including purpose, parameters, steps, and flow diagram

prerequisites: Clear understanding of the workflow to be templated
Knowledge of existing templates and steps
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: review requirements → check existing → purpose → use cases → check reusable steps → plan steps → identify parameters → design flow → create diagram
Before planning steps: Check existing generic steps in ~/.claude/zeremai/steps/planning/ and ~/.claude/zeremai/steps/common/
When planning steps: Prefer reusable step categories
When planning steps: Ensure each step represents actual work, not flow control
Use camelCase for parameter names: featureName, targetBranch
tools: read_file - Read existing templates and steps
list_dir - Explore existing templates and step categories
bestPractices: Check existing templates before creating new ones

STEP REUSE FIRST: Before proposing ANY new step, explicitly search existing steps (planning/, common/, investigation/, learning/) to see if they can handle the use case with different parameters or scope. Only propose a new step after confirming no existing step can be adapted.
Keep templates focused on a single workflow
Always include continuous improvement as final step with approvalRequired: true
Use clear parameter naming with camelCase
Design steps to produce tangible outputs
Ensure flow diagram matches step sequence
Ask the user within steps, not as standalone steps - use the AskUserQuestion tool (see askUserAsSubstepPattern)
Design feedback loops for iterative flows - allow returning to gather more info (see feedbackLoopsPattern)
For templates coordinating multiple phases/skills, use orchestrator pattern (see orchestratorPattern)
Prefer native flow templates over skill wrappers for sub-flows — native templates get full flow tracking, memory, logging, and continuous improvement (see nativeOverSkillWrappersPattern)
Orchestrator templates should be pure sequencing — no direct work steps (like context gathering) when sub-flows handle their own context

orchestratorPattern.description: Use an orchestrator template when coordinating multiple independent phases, each with its own workflow, approval gates, and context gathering
whenToUse: Template coordinates 3+ phases that each have their own multi-step workflow
Phases can evolve independently and be reused standalone
Different phases may be added or removed over time
Each phase needs its own approval gates and flow tracking
howToImplement: Orchestrator template steps use subFlowTrigger metadata to declare which sub-flow to spawn (stepRef is null)
Each phase is a separate sub-flow template with its own steps
Use syncPoint: immediate for sequential phase execution
Orchestrator only has: sub-flow spawning steps + continuous-improvement + complete-flow
Do NOT add context-gathering steps to the orchestrator — sub-flows gather their own context
Keep orchestrator parameters minimal — only what's needed to identify the work (e.g., workItemId)
orchestratorPattern.antiPattern: Adding direct work steps (context gathering, analysis) to the orchestrator when sub-flows already handle those concerns

nativeOverSkillWrappersPattern.description: When a sub-flow needs to replicate what a skill does, convert the skill logic to native flow steps rather than invoking the skill
nativeOverSkillWrappersPattern.rationale: Skill invocations are opaque — the flow framework cannot track individual decisions, log substep progress, or apply continuous improvement. Native templates get full flow tracking at every substep.
whenToUse: Sub-flow needs to replicate a skill's workflow
Flow tracking and approval gates are needed at the substep level
The workflow needs to evolve independently through continuous improvement
howToImplement: Read the skill definition to understand its full workflow
Break the skill's workflow into flow steps with clear inputs/outputs
Embed skill-specific rules into step guidance
Add approval gates where the skill had user confirmation points
nativeOverSkillWrappersPattern.antiPattern: Creating a single step that just invokes /skill-name — this bypasses flow tracking

askUserAsSubstepPattern.description: Ask the user within steps rather than creating standalone question steps
askUserAsSubstepPattern.rationale: Questions to the user naturally occur during multiple steps - a standalone question step is artificial and creates unnecessary flow overhead
askUserAsSubstepPattern.sharedSkill: the AskUserQuestion tool for structured questions
whenToUse: Information gaps are discovered during step execution
User clarification is needed before proceeding
howToImplement: Do NOT create a standalone question step in the template
Instead, add asking the user as a substep within relevant steps
Use the AskUserQuestion tool for structured questions
Steps that commonly need to ask the user: context understanding, information gathering, design creation

substeps.name: Ask the user (if needed)
substeps.description: Use the AskUserQuestion tool to gather missing information

askUserAsSubstepPattern.antiPattern: Creating a dedicated 'Question Step' or 'Answer Open Questions' step in the template flow

feedbackLoopsPattern.description: Design flow flows that can loop back to earlier steps when additional information or work is needed
feedbackLoopsPattern.rationale: During analysis or creation phases, gaps are often discovered that require returning to information gathering. Rigid linear flows force workarounds or incomplete work.
whenToUse: Analysis steps may reveal missing information
Creation/design steps may need additional context
Validation steps may require corrections in earlier outputs
howToImplement: Identify steps that commonly discover information gaps (analysis, design, creation)
Add conditional return paths to information gathering steps
In mermaid diagram: add decision diamonds with 'Need more info?' branches
Document the feedback loop trigger conditions in step descriptions
feedbackLoopsPattern.mermaidExample:
graph TD
    A[Gather Info] --> B[Analyze]
    B --> C{Info Complete?}
    C -->|No| A
    C -->|Yes| D[Create Design]
    D --> E{Gaps Found?}
    E -->|Yes| A
    E -->|No| F[Done]
feedbackLoopsPattern.antiPattern: Forcing strictly linear flows where steps cannot revisit earlier work when needed

substeps.name: Review requirements
substeps.description: Understand what workflow needs to be templated
actions: Review the stated need for a new template
Identify the workflow to be standardized

substeps.name: Check existing templates
substeps.description: Verify no similar template already exists
actions: Identify templates that could be extended vs creating new

substeps.name: Write purpose statement
substeps.description: Define clear purpose for the template
actions: Describe what workflow the template enables
Ensure purpose is specific and actionable

substeps.name: Define use cases
substeps.description: Document when to use this template

substeps.name: Check existing reusable steps
substeps.description: Identify steps that can be reused
actions: List existing steps that fit the workflow

substeps.name: Plan step breakdown
actions: FOR EACH STAGE: First search existing steps that could handle the requirement with different parameters/scope before proposing a new step
Assign steps to each stage (strongly prefer reusing existing steps)
Define expected output for each step
Ensure each step produces tangible work
Identify which steps need user approval before proceeding (mark with approvalRequired: true)

substeps.name: Identify parameters
actions: Identify values that must be provided by user (required)
Identify values that are helpful but optional

substeps.name: Design flow flow
substeps.description: Map out the logical flow of the template
actions: Plan sync points if sub-flows involved
Consider feedback loops: Can analysis/creation steps return to gather more info? (see feedbackLoopsPattern)

substeps.name: Create mermaid diagram
actions: Include all steps and decision points

substeps.name: End-Step: Log Problems
substeps.description: Log what went wrong in this step
actions: Log problems: If any problems, errors, workarounds, or unexpected situations were encountered during this step, log them via add-log-entry --problems '["description of problem 1", ...]'. This feeds the continuous-improvement step's analysis.

flow.description: Linear flow through all 9 substeps: requirements → existing check → purpose → use cases → reusable steps → step breakdown → parameters → flow design → diagram

fields: Information Produced: Purpose statement, parameters list, step breakdown, flow diagram
Decisions Made: Step organization, parameter choices, reusable step selections
